=={{header|FreeBASIC}}==
FreeBASIC already has the unary operator <code>Sgn</code> built in, but it doesn't work with signed zeros.

In FreeBASIC, floating-point numbers do not distinguish between +0.0 and -0.0 in standard comparisons (x = 0), since both are represented internally as 0 with no explicit sign. However, bit manipulation (for Single or Double types) preserves the sign in specific contexts (e.g., advanced mathematical operations or sign-sensitive algorithms).
<syntaxhighlight lang="vbnet">Function Signum(x As Single) As Single
    Dim As Integer Ptr p = @x ' Pointer to the underlying integer of the Single
    Dim As Integer signBit = (*p And &h80000000)
    ' &h80000000 isolates bit 31 (sign bit in IEEE 754).
    ' If x is negative (or -0.0), signBit will be &h80000000; If it is positive (or +0.0), it will be 0.
    
    If x = 0 Then
        Dim As Single result = 0.0
        Dim As Integer Ptr pResult = @result
        *pResult = signBit ' Write the sign bit to the result
        Return result
    Elseif x < 0 Then
        Return -1.0
    Else
        Return 1.0
    End If
End Function</syntaxhighlight>
